restoration_note: Two-movement teaching: (1) cosmographic scaffolding (pillars, sea, four bearing-angels, twelve/twenty-two angels, Omophoros, firmaments, Five Sons as 'food of the man'), and (2) the doctrinal answer identifying the liturgical Yes/Amen with the Calling/Hearing. The first half is heavily damaged with mostly large line-opening and line-end lacunae carrying no formulaic constraint; these I leave unrestored. The second half (122.4–26) is well-anchored by the Call/Answer parallel and standard Manichaean phrasing, so the editor's restorations can be confirmed with high confidence. Selected catalogue completions (cosmos-spelling, paiskos, stylos, twelve heavens-below, ten omophoroi etc.) are restorable from glossary forms and surviving partial traces. Gaps with no traces or only single-letter partials are honestly marked unrestorable.

restorations.basis: 30-char line opening with only the ending -ⲭⲟⲥ visible (likely a Greek loanword in -αρχος); list-context (great X with great Y) gives no formulaic constraint, multiple candidates equally possible.
15-char line end after ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ-; could be any of several governed nouns in the catalogue (ⲛⲟⲩⲥ, ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ, ⲡⲛⲁ); not constrained.
30-char line opening with no surviving traces; multiple ways to begin a 'with the Great Mind' clause.
15-char line end after ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ 'which exists'; the locative complement (ⲍⲙ̄/ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈/ⲁⲍⲣⲏ ⲡⲧⲏⲣⲉⲥ etc.) is not constrained.
30-char line opening before 'the Youth (Jesus the Radiance)'; introductory clause cannot be reconstructed from the surviving text.
15-char line end with partial ⲡⲛ-; could be ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ('great Pillar' under which the Youth stands) or ⲡⲛⲁ ('Spirit'); possibilities not narrow enough.
30-char line opening with no traces.
15-char line end after 'the twelve angels'; their attribute or function not preserved.
30-char line opening with no traces.
15-char line end after 'the twenty-two angels'; attribute not preserved.
30-char line opening; not constrained.
15-char line end; the predicate of the two distinct angels not preserved.
3-char line opening before 'the seven pillars that stand fast'; the catalogue is a list of cosmic structures connected with ⲙⲛ̄ 'and / together with' (parallel to ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ in 121.42–43).
Confirms editor: ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand fast' is the standard Lycopolitan idiom (cf. 5517 ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲩ); ⲡⲥⲁϣϩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲉⲧⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ = 'seven pillars that stand fast.'
3-char line opening introducing the next item in the catalogue (sea); ⲙⲛ̄ continues the list-pattern.
Confirms editor: ⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ (θάλασσα) 'sea'; the 2-char restoration ⲑⲁ- yields the standard Greek loanword for the sea encircling the cosmos (glossary: ⲛⲑⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ/ⲫⲁⲗⲁⲥⲥⲁ).
4-char line end after directional ⲁ-; the noun governed (heavens, earth, etc.) not constrained.
Confirms editor: ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ = 'the four' (glossary numeral); the four bearing-angels are a recurring motif (the Four Faces of Light / four bearers of the cosmos).

4-char line end after ⲁⲧⲡ-; could be ⲁⲧⲡⲉ 'to heaven' or ⲁⲧⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'to below', but the next line begins ⲥⲙⲟⲥ (i.e. cosmos split across the line break) which makes the simple ⲁⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ reading inconsistent with the visible ⲁⲧⲡ. Insufficient constraint.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ split across the line break.
4-char line end after 'under the strength of'; possible candidates (ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ, ⲡⲓⲱⲧ, ⲡⲡⲛⲁ) all fit but none is uniquely required.
3-char line opening; relative continuation could be many things.
Completes ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ 'all of them' (per apparatus partial trace ⲧⲏⲣⲟ-); standard Lycopolitan idiom 'all the heavens, all of them.'
3-char line opening with no traces.
4-char line end with ⲛⲉⲧ- relative; predicate of the Five Sons ('food of the man') not preserved.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ split across the line break.

10-char abraded stretch between ⲛ̄ and ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ; the connecting phrase ('at the X of the Calling' or 'at the time/place/sound of the Calling') is the doctrinal hinge of the chapter but the specific noun is not preserved.
Confirms editor: the cosmic Call/Answer formula pairs ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ + ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ; ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ '(and) the Hearing' continues the standard dyad.
8-char illegible stretch between Hearing and Radiance; the connecting phrase not preserved.
4-char line end after 'the Radiance of the'; could be ⲡⲣⲏ 'sun' (Jesus the Radiance is associated with the sun) or ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glory'; not narrowly constrained.
Completes ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the Light' (per apparatus partial trace ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛ-); 'the Adamas of the Light' = ⲡⲁⲇⲁⲙⲁⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ in glossary.
10-char abraded line opening.
5-char line end with partial ⲛ̄ⲭ- (Lycopolitan ⲭ for Sahidic ϫ); function-word too short to constrain.
3-char fragment with partial ⲁⲭ- and English 'steering her'; the steered feminine (ship, sphere, sea) and the verb form not jointly determinable.

3-char gap between ⲛ and ⲉ; ⲛⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'the heavens' (Lycopolitan plural in -ⲉ) gives 'the heavens which are below' — the firmamental sphere in which the twelve powers (the zodiacal twelve) stand. Glossary anchor: ⲛⲙⲧⲏⲩⲉ already attested in this chapter (5515) as 'heavens'.
Confirms editor: ⲁϩⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'stand on the feet of' — standard Lycopolitan idiom continued across the line break with ⲣⲉⲧ[ⲟ]ⲩ on the next line.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲣⲉⲧⲟⲩ 'their feet' bridging from previous line (continuation of ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲟⲩ idiom).
4-char line end after 'the count of the twelve likenesses'; the predicate (e.g. ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ 'of...' + governed noun) not narrowly determinable.
5-char line end after 'three great pillars of strength which'; the predicate is plausibly ⲉⲩⲃⲓ ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'bear up' (echoing 5514, 5526) but the exact form/length is not certain.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ 'pillars'.
Confirms editor: ⲡⲁⲓⲥⲕⲟⲥ (the cosmic disc/shield borne by the Omophoros) is the standard reading; the trace ⲡⲁ-ⲥⲕⲟⲥ requires a single ⲓ.
3-char gap between ⲡⲁⲓⲥⲕⲟⲥ and 'the other three'; connector (ⲙⲛ̄/ⲁⲩⲱ) plausible but not strictly constrained.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲡⲕⲉϣⲁⲙⲧ 'the other three' (the three great pillars).
5-char gap with partial ⲛ̄ϩⲏ-; could be ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧⲥ̄ + further short word, but not securely reconstructable.
4-char line end with ⲉⲧ- relative; the verb of the Spirit (e.g. ⲉⲧⲁϩⲣ̄... 'has placed') is split with line 66 but the exact morphology is not preserved.
5-char gap with opening syllable ⲃⲁ-; verb fragment without narrow constraint.
6-char line end after 'at that very hour'; continuation not preserved.
5-char gap with partial ⲛⲧ-; not constrained.
4-char gap with ⲛⲙⲡ- ('and the'); the noun 'which are sown' could be ⲃⲣⲉⲩⲉ 'seeds' (glossary) but the morphological fit is uncertain.
3-char gap with directional ⲁϩⲁⲛ-; the governed noun not preserved.
4-char fragment after -ⲗⲟⲥ ending (probably ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ or ⲁⲅⲅⲉⲗⲟⲥ); the relative phrase that follows is too short to anchor.
3-char gap; not constrained.
1-char gap inside ⲡⲓⲕ?ⲛⲉ; could be ⲡⲓⲕⲁⲛⲉ vel sim. but not a known glossary form here.
3-char line end after ⲛⲉ; not constrained.
4-char gap with opening ϩ-; not constrained.
8-char abraded line end after 'the perfection of this ten'; likely refers to ten omophoroi or similar but the noun is not preserved.
6-char line opening; introductory connector to 'great Omophoros' is not securely constrained.
6-char gap after Omophoros with no traces.
4-char gap with opening syllable ⲛⲕ-; not constrained.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ split across the line break.
30-char destroyed remainder of line plus next line; nothing recoverable.
3-char line opening before 'these are the three great...'; could be ⲁⲩⲱ 'and' but not securely.

8-char line end after 'three great' with ⲛ̄ genitive opening; the chapter has already named ⲡϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ 'three great pillars' twice (5525, 5526), so the summarizing 'these are the three great [pillars]' is the natural fill. Length matches.
3-char gap with opening ⲙ-; not constrained.
14-char illegible line end after 'against'; the opposed entity not preserved.
5-char line opening before 'a name'; could be 'tell us' or 'give us' formula but the surviving traces (only two dots) do not constrain.
5-char line end after 'the Blessed One' (= Father of Greatness); continuation not preserved.
3-char line opening before 'shall be blessed'; subject (ⲡⲣⲉⲛ 'the name' or relative) plausible but not narrowly forced.
Confirms editor: ⲡϣⲗⲏⲗ ⲉⲧⲛⲁϣⲗⲏⲗ ⲛⲍⲏⲧϥ 'the prayer that shall be prayed unto him' — standard liturgical phrasing referring to the Blessed One.
Confirms editor: ⲡⲍⲁⲙⲏⲛ 'the Amen'; the Yes/Amen pair is the central question of the chapter.
Confirms editor: ⲡⲍⲁⲙⲏⲛ; same as 5538.
Confirms editor: ⲛ̄- relative prefix on ⲧⲁϩϣⲱⲡⲉ 'which have come into being'.
Confirms editor: ⲁⲩ†ⲣ[ⲛⲧϩ ⲁ]/[ⲣ]ⲁϩ 'they were given a name [unto him]'; bridge to ⲁⲣⲁϩ on the next line.
Confirms editor: ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'unto him' continued from previous line.
Confirms editor: parallel structure 'the Yes is reckoned (ⲏⲡ ⲁ-) to the Calling, the Amen [reckoned to] the Answer'; the parallel is required by the doctrinal answer in 5542.
Confirms editor: final ⲉ of ⲡⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ + ⲙ̄ⲛ 'and' joining Calling + Hearing.
Confirms editor: ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲩ 'they are' continuation.
Confirms editor: ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' completing the petitioning-forth phrase.

Confirms editor: ⲣⲣⲟ 'reigned' + ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲉⲉⲩⲉ 'in the thought'; the cosmic-faculty register fits the assertion that Yes/Amen are not the high reigning ones (Father, Mother, First Man) but acted on their behalf.
Confirms editor: ⲡⲱⲛⲍ 'Life'; the standard pair 'Father of Life and Father of those who live' (ⲡⲓⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄) is the lexicon entry for Father of Greatness.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the First Man' (lexicon).
Confirms editor: ⲁⲛ 'also/again' continuing the parallel — the Mother of Life [also] sought; reading flows into 5547 'Mother of Life and Father of those who live sought.'
3-char gap with both flanks fragmentary; the verbal complement in 'sought ... M-' (presumably introducing the Aromaios on next line) not securely reconstructable.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲣⲣⲟ + ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ 'reigned over/of' governing 'these Aeons'.
Confirms editor: ⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'soul' (with † for ⲯ in this scribal hand); confirmed by line 21's 'mingled with Death' which is precisely the captured soul state.
Confirms editor: initial ⲙ of ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄ 'mingled' (lexicon: Mingling, ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄).
3-char gap with partial ⲕ and English '... helpers ... of the [first man]'; could be ⲛ̄ⲕⲁ 'companions' or 'kindred' but not precisely fixed.

6-char gap with partial ⲉ . . ⲁⲣ; 'they gave him to ...' but the recipient phrase (likely Mother of Life or Father of the Living, given the next line) is not narrowly determinable from visible traces.
5-char gap; the connecting phrase between 'Mother of Life' and 'they are refiners of the Living Soul' not preserved.
Confirms editor: ⲉⲩϣⲟⲟⲡ 'being' — qualitative-of-existence governing ⲛ̄ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲟⲥ 'helpers' on the next line.
Confirms editor: completion of ⲃⲟⲏⲑⲟⲥ 'helpers' bridging from the previous line.
5-char line end after 'whether thus in'; presumably an ⲉⲓⲧⲉ-pair element (parallel to the next line's 'in the tree, in the fashioning of the flesh'), but the specific noun is not preserved.

2-char line opening before 'in the tree, or in the fashioning of the flesh'; the ⲉⲓⲧⲉ ... ⲉⲓⲧⲉ ... pattern of the preceding line (5557: ⲉⲓⲧⲉ ⲃⲉ ⲍⲙ̄ ...) calls for a connector here, but the exact 2-letter form is uncertain.
3-char gap after 'flesh of the' — could be ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'man' (4 chars) or another short noun; not certainly determinable.
